content.title: About
content.content: Broccoflower is a hybrid vegetable created by crossing broccoli and cauliflower. It looks like a cauliflower head with bright green florets. It is eaten raw, offering a mild nutty flavor and a crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoflower was first developed in the 1990s in the United States.
It combines the nutritional benefits of both parent vegetables – broccoli and cauliflower.
The vivid green color comes from high chlorophyll levels, enhanced by ample light during growth.
Broccoflower is often featured in culinary shows as an “exotic” vegetable.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Provides over 100 % of the daily value for vitamin C, which supports immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Broccoflower contains glucosinolates and carotenoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to cruciferous vegetables
items.content: People allergic to broccoli, cauliflower, or other crucifers may react to broccoflower.

items.title: Hard-to-digest fibers
items.content: High fiber content can cause gas and bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: As with most fresh produce, residues may be present; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Broccoflower can be eaten raw in salads, thinly sliced in wraps, or added to smoothies. It can also be briefly blanched to soften the texture while retaining most nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container or a perforated bag. It stays fresh for 5–7 days. Discard if yellow spots or off‑odors develop.
